text_blocks.snippet: Managed detection and response (MDR) is a 24/7 outsourced cybersecurity service that combines security tools, analytics, and human expertise to detect, investigate, and actively respond to threats.
snippet_highlighted_words: a 24/7 outsourced cybersecurity service that combines security tools, analytics, and human expertise to detect, investigate, and actively respond to threats

text_blocks.snippet: MDR providers monitor telemetry across your entire infrastructure—including endpoints, networks, cloud workloads, identity systems, and email—using platforms like EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) or XDR (Extended Detection and Response).

list.snippet: Prioritize: Sifts through high volumes of alerts and filters out false positives.
Hunt: Proactively searches for hidden threats, stealthy malware, or lateral movement that automated tools miss.
Investigate: Analyzes the severity, scope, and root cause of suspicious behavior.
Remediate & Neutralize: Isolates compromised hosts, blocks active attacks, and provides guidance or direct action to restore systems.
Around-the-Clock Coverage: Provides continuous 24/7/365 surveillance without requiring you to build or expand an in-house Security Operations Center (SOC).
Skills Gap Relief: Solves talent shortages by giving resource-constrained teams direct access to elite security analysts and threat intelligence.
Faster Response Times: Shrinks threat dwell time from weeks or months down to minutes through active containment.
MDR vs. EDR: EDR is a software tool that monitors endpoint devices; MDR is the human-led service that operates EDR and handles investigation and response.

MDR vs. MSSP: Traditional Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs) typically focus on device maintenance, log collection, and pushing alerts to your team. MDR focuses on active threat disruption, investigation, and actual remediation.
MDR vs. XDR: XDR provides the underlying multi-layer detection technology, while MDR is the managed service layer (often built on top of XDR) that supplies the analysts.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more about definitions and provider models through Microsoft Security and Palo Alto Networks.
